parts.prompt: Prove that for any positive numbers $p$ and $q$: $$p + q \ge \sqrt{4pq}$$

markScheme.text: Expands $(p+q)^2$ and writes it as $(p-q)^2 + 4pq$, or an equivalent rearrangement
States and uses the fact that $(p-q)^2 \ge 0$
Takes the positive square root, valid because $p+q>0$, to conclude $p+q \ge \sqrt{4pq}$

llm.context: Accept any rigorous equivalent method, for example starting from $(\sqrt{p}-\sqrt{q})^2 \ge 0$. The final A1 requires a concluding statement.

hint.content: Both sides are positive, so it is enough to compare their squares. What do you know about $(p-q)^2$?

solution.content: Both sides are positive because $p, q > 0$, so taking the positive square root gives $$p + q \ge \sqrt{4pq}$$ as required.
